title: Branch on the most fractional variable

blocks.text: The crew-rostering search branches on the first fractional variable it sees, and the team wants to try the most-fractional rule instead.

Write `most_fractional(x, tol=1e-6)` in `most_fractional.py`. `x` maps each integer variable's name to its LP value; values may be above 1 (counts of crews). A variable is a candidate when its value is more than `tol` from the nearest whole number. Among the candidates, return the name with the largest
the distance from $`x_j`$ to the nearer whole number. Ties go to the variable listed first in `x`. Return `None` when there is no candidate.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from most_fractional import most_fractional

print("open 0.85, crews 2.4, vans 1.0:", most_fractional({"open": 0.85, "crews": 2.4, "vans": 1.0}))
print("open 0.25, crews 1.75:", most_fractional({"open": 0.25, "crews": 1.75}))
print("open 1.0, crews 3.0000001:", most_fractional({"open": 1.0, "crews": 3.0000001}))

cases.says: a solution of whole numbers has nothing to branch on, so the answer is None
0.25 and 0.75 are equally fractional, and the first one listed wins
a count of 3.5 is more fractional than 0.4: only the part after the whole number counts
a value within the tolerance of a whole number is never chosen
